group_assessment.weighting: A single-subject investigator-sponsored report (PubMed type Case Reports) of an intra-cisterna-magna AAV9 IDUA programme under a four-drug immunosuppression protocol. It carries a regimen and a schedule of assessments that the protocol supplement prints; it carries no nerve conduction study, no ganglion imaging and no tissue. It can bear on 'was a sensory-ganglion endpoint measured under immunosuppression' and on nothing about WWOX.

verbatim_locators.source_fulltext_indexed_evidence: JATS from E-utilities efetch db=pmc. Body separated from front matter by the reader's own extraction; every locator is matched against the normalised body text of the declared artefact.
verbatim_locators.abstract_anchoring_waived: No locator draws on the abstract; every entry is matched against the body.
verbatim_locators.note: Coverage: abstract, introduction, Results (clinical history, clinical outcomes, adverse events, biochemical outcomes, serologies, neurodevelopmental outcomes), Discussion and Materials and methods read from the JATS running text. Figure panels were NOT rendered: the numbers carried are stated in running text and quoted from there, and the one figure-derived locator is explicitly marked caption_only. Supplementary Video S1 and Documents S1-S3 (protocol, Tables S1-S3) were not fetched, so the 23-event adverse-event listing is receipted only as the running text's summary of Table S3.

entries.proposition: THE HUMAN INTRACISTERNAL DOSE LITERAL IS PRINTED WITH AN IMPOSSIBLE SIGN AND MUST NOT BE CARRIED AS PRINTED: a negative exponent of vector genome copies per gram of brain mass would denote a fraction of one genome copy. The paper's own paired figures recover the intended magnitudes by division; the printed form has lost the superscripts in both abstract and body.
entries.snippet: Following successful computed tomography (CT)-guided access to the cisterna magna with a 25-gauge neonatal spinal needle, 1E−10 vector genome copies/g brain mass (1.265E−13 genome copies) of RGX-111 in 5 mL of Elliotts B artificial CSF was injected over 5 min without adverse effects.

entries.proposition: DORSAL ROOT GANGLION TOXICITY WAS NOT MEASURED IN THIS HUMAN RECIPIENT: the authors state plainly that no nerve conduction studies were performed, and rest the inference on absence of reported paraesthesia and on deep tendon reflexes in a child dosed in the second year of life.
entries.snippet: Although no formal nerve conduction studies were performed, due to the protocol being a treatment investigational new drug (IND), the subject did not complain of paresthesias and did not demonstrate abnormal deep tendon reflexes, suggesting there was no clinically significant dorsal root ganglion (DRG) toxicity.

entries.proposition: THE ADVERSE EVENT BURDEN OF THIS PROCEDURE IS ATTRIBUTED BY THE INVESTIGATORS MAINLY TO THE IMMUNOSUPPRESSION RATHER THAN TO THE VECTOR.
entries.snippet: In total, 23 adverse events have been recorded to date (see Table S3); 17 occurred in the first year following dosing, and 16 of those were assessed to be possibly related to immunosuppression.

entries.proposition: TRANSGENE PRODUCT IN CSF DECLINED AFTER IMMUNOSUPPRESSION WAS WEANED, SO DURABILITY AND NOT ONLY TOXICITY HAS A MODIFIABLE IMMUNE COMPONENT ON THIS ROUTE.
entries.snippet: (A) CSF IDUA enzyme levels measured over 290 weeks suggest rapid-onset IDUA transgene expression (week 8), which peaked at 35 weeks and subsequently declined after weaning of immunosuppression began (blue arrow).

entries.proposition: THE CSF AND PLASMA ANTIBODY COMPARTMENTS ARE NOT EQUILIBRATED AFTER A DIRECT CNS DOSE.
entries.snippet: Note that despite direct CNS dosing of RGX-111, the ratio of plasma to CSF anti-IDUA titers obtained at the same time ranged from 320:1 to 1,280:1.

entries.proposition: A TUMOUR WITH VECTOR GENOME INTEGRATION AFTER THE SAME ROUTE AND VECTOR IN A DIFFERENT CHILD IS CARRIED BY THIS PAPER AS A CITATION, NOT AS ITS OWN FINDING; IT IS AN OPEN READING DEBT.
entries.snippet: Finally, given the recent identification of an intraventricular CNS tumor demonstrating vector genome integration in a 5-year-old severe MPS I patient who had received ICM RGX-111 in the phase 1/2 open-label study (NCT03580083) at age 1 year,10 the absence of brain or spine neoplasms in our child more than 5.5 years post RGX-111 is important to note.

entries.proposition: The supplemental protocol schedules physical and neurologic examination (immediately after dosing, day 1, then 8, 24, 56, 78, 104 weeks) and brain MRI at 56 and 104 weeks; it names no nerve conduction study, no spine or ganglion imaging and no tissue sampling.
entries.snippet: Physical and neurologic examination will occur immediately following, and one day after RGX-111 dosing.

entries.proposition: Brain MRI is scheduled at 56 and 104 weeks only in the protocol; the article reports annual brain MRI and says annual brain and spine MRI surveillance continues.
entries.snippet: Brain magnetic resonance imaging will be performed at 56 and 104 weeks post-RGX-111 dosing.

entries.proposition: The protocol lists four adjunctive immunosuppressive drugs: a single intravenous methylprednisolone dose, oral prednisone tapered to week 12, tacrolimus to week 32 and sirolimus for 48 weeks.
entries.snippet: Sirolimus, 1 mg/m2 every 4 hours x 3 doses, 2 days prior to RGX-111 administration

entries.proposition: Tacrolimus is dosed from the day after vector administration with titration, and sirolimus starts two days before.
entries.snippet: Tacrolimus, 0.05 mg/kg/dose orally, twice daily starting day following RGX-111 administration

entries.proposition: Tacrolimus is discontinued by week 32 and only sirolimus levels are drawn at 32 and 40 weeks.
entries.snippet:
Since tacrolimus will be discontinued by week 32, only sirolimus levels will
be obtained at 32 and 40 weeks

entries.proposition: Table S3 lists the 23 adverse events with causality columns including relation to immunosuppression; none of its listed terms is a sensory, neurologic or spinal term (a term search for neuro*, gait, weak*, tremor, seizure, headache, ataxi*, paresis, reflex, hypotonia, spinal, lumbar, nerve returned 0; the sensory/pain search returned one musculoskeletal knee-pain row).
entries.snippet: Table S3. Listing of adverse events with complete details including causality assessments and outcome.

entries.proposition: Figure 2 shows plasma anti-IDUA antibody titre falling on immunosuppression then surging to its highest point between roughly one and two years after withdrawal, then returning to low levels; CSF titre dips then returns to its baseline value before falling.
entries.snippet: [panel attestation - Fig. 2 raster inspected] Panel A plasma: baseline high, down during immunosuppression, rise after the blue arrow to the top of the axis near 102,400 around weeks 85-105, back to low values by about week 180. Panel B CSF: 80 at baseline, 40, 40, back to 80 at about week 60, then 10 and 20 at about weeks 225 and 275.

entries.proposition: Figure 1 shows single-subject CSF IDUA (peak then decline, ending below the control scatter), CSF heparan sulfate (fall then plateau above the control distribution) and urine GAGs; every panel is a biochemical readout and none is a sensory, electrophysiological or imaging readout.
entries.snippet: [panel attestation - Fig. 1 raster inspected] A CSF IDUA vs 17 control samples; B CSF HS vs control box; C total urinary GAG with an age-stepped reference line; D urinary HS and DS with reference lines; n = 1 subject; blue arrow marks the start of immunosuppression withdrawal.

entries.proposition: Figure 3 plots age-equivalent scores for cognition, expressive communication and fine motor against chronologic age; no sensory or nerve readout.
entries.snippet: [panel attestation - Fig. 3 raster inspected] Three panels of age-equivalent months versus chronologic months with shaded bands around identity; a second dataset (orange) appears in the cognitive panel only.
